notes: The supplied PDF has only the cover and the step pages. The parts-inventory pages with Element IDs were not included, so piece types are inferred from the pictures and the closest catalogue entries.

Colours are given in props. Several catalogue entries have a different catalogue colour. The chassis uses lego-4210997 (listed as black) for a dark grey plate. The red 2x4 plates use lego-302026 (black), and the red 1x4 front plate uses lego-4107758 (green). The red roof plate uses lego-4211186 (brown). I chose them because they have enough distinct studs and anti-studs, since each stud and anti-stud port can only be used once.
I did not model the rear mudguard shape in step 3. I used a plain red 2x4 plate for the rear deck.

Each stud or anti-stud port is used by only one join. I assigned a different stud.N or anti-stud.N to each connection. The exact stud positions are not visible in the pictures, so the numbering is arbitrary.
The two wheel-holder plates sit under the chassis. The chassis has only one anti-stud port, so those two joins leave the chassis port null.
In step 3 the red front deck is already on the chassis in the picture, although only the rear red piece is shown being added. I assumed a red 2x4 plate at the front and one at the rear.
Step 5 shows a sub-assembly: a red plate with grille and headlights. I attached it to the front deck.
Step 6 adds black plates in the middle. I modelled them as one black 1x2 plate.
Step 8's trans-clear windscreen bricks and red 1x1 bricks are placed on the chassis and rear deck. Step 9 adds the red roof plate and four wheels.
Each wheel holder carries two wheels, and the catalogue entry has only one pin port. Both wheels on a holder are joined to its pin.1 (pin ports can be shared).
